description:
FOUND s461aq, probing #77's return-family battery (row 10); PRE-EXISTING â
the base tree (33a71c9) answers identically, so it is NOT #77's.

    sub maybe { my $n = shift; return $n + 1 if $n > 0 }
    my $y = maybe(-1);
    print defined $y ? "def" : "undef", "\n";
    # perl: def      PCL: undef

A sub that falls off the end returns the value of the LAST STATEMENT
EVALUATED.  When that statement is `return EXPR if COND` with COND false, the
statement's own value is the false CONDITION â "" â which is DEFINED.  PCL
lowers the modifier to `(p-if COND (p-return â¦))` and an untaken `p-if`
yields undef.

The BLOCK spelling is already right: `sub m2 { my $n=shift; if ($n>0) { return $n+1 } }`
answers "def" on both (probed).  So this is the statement-modifier lowering
only â `_apply_modifier`'s `['p-if', $cond, $form]` needs the perl rule that
an untaken statement modifier's value is the condition's value, not undef.

SIZE: unknown; the fix is one arm in `_apply_modifier`, but "the value of an
untaken modifier" has to be probed for `unless`/`while`/`until` too before it
is written.  Cheap discriminating measurement: `perl -e 'sub f { 1 if 0 }
print defined f() ? "d" : "u"'` for each modifier word.

NOT BLOCKING anything measured: no baseline row moves on it (found by probe,
not by a failing test).

=== SHIPPED s463au (agent AU, round 20).  CLOSED.

THE TASK ASKED FOR THE SIBLING SHAPES FIRST, AND THAT IS WHAT SIZED IT.
Probed 5.40.3 (25 rows): an untaken `if`/`unless` STATEMENT MODIFIER
evaluates to the CONDITION'S OWN VALUE â `""` for a false comparison, `0` for
a literal 0, undef for a literal undef â and `unless` yields the condition
too, NOT its negation (`sub { 5 unless 1 }` is 1).  So the rule is not about
`return` at all.

THE TASK'S OWN CLUE WAS THE ANSWER: it says the BLOCK spelling
`if (C) { return X }` is already right.  That is because the block form has
always used the ret-var transform (`let --pcl-if-ret--N`: the condition into
the temp, the body over it when taken), and the MODIFIER form used it for a
plain expression tail only.  Four other routes reached a bare `p-if`:

    return X if C           _lower_stmt's Statement::Break branch
    next/last/goto if C     the same branch's tail
    our $y = 5 if C         _lower_our_decl
    my ($a,$b) = â¦ if C     the declaration's $assign_form
    my $x = 5 if C          the scalar-declaration branch, which spelled
                            `['p-if', $cf, $set]` INLINE â a fourth copy

WHAT SHIPPED.  `_modifier_ret_form` is the one spelling of the shape;
`_apply_modifier` takes an optional `$tail_ctx` and applies it, so a caller
that KNOWS it is in tail position opts in with one argument.  The
plain-expression site keeps its own call to the helper because the two sites
lower in a different ORDER â it lowers the CONDITION first, the `return`
family lowers its EXPRESSION first â so the ret-var NAME is allocated by the
caller and that site's emission is byte-identical.

THE GATE IS TAIL POSITION, which is what keeps the change small: a modifier
whose value is discarded keeps the bare `p-if`, so every early
`return â¦ if â¦` in the middle of a sub is untouched.  Measured: 4 files move
out of 1145.

BARS MET.  corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111; emission A/B over 1145 files
SAME=1141 DIFF=4 RCDIFF=0 with all four probed against perl (Test-Simple
Legacy/More.t + Legacy/Builder/is_fh.t â BOOLEAN consumers, so their answers
are unchanged and only `defined`/list-arity move, toward perl; Text::CSV_PP's
`last if !defined $c` at a do-while lambda tail plus one ret-var RENUMBER;
t/re/pat_advanced.t).  FULL SWEEP GATE clean, TOTAL 18346 -> 18346 (+0), no
per-file pass delta.  COMPANION: the one suite file whose emission moved is
re/pat_advanced.t, which `--quick` does not run â run ALONE at --timeout 900
it is 951/729, exactly its snapshot row.  45 probe rows across three
batteries.  Guard `Pl/t/stmt-modifier-01.t` 39 -> 44, inverse-verified on
6e6f191.  Generation v2-581 + the three artifacts.

ONE RESIDUE, and it is deliberate: `sub { return X while 0 }` is `0` in perl
and `""` in PCL.  The `while`/`until`/`for` modifiers take the v1 fallback
path (`_modifier_needs_fallback`), and perl's value there is an optree
artifact its own twin contradicts â `sub { return X until 1 }` is `""` in
perl, which PCL already matches.  Not worth a mechanism.
subject: `return EXPR if COND;` with a FALSE condition yields undef in PCL, "" in perl
